newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Police fire in air to break up Indonesian protest.
newsitem.headline: Police fire in air to break up Indonesian protest.

text.p: Police fired into the air on Saturday to disperse an angry crowd during a political campaign demonstration in a suburb of the Indonesian capital, Jakarta, witnesses said.
Witnesses said supporters of the minority Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) tried to force their way into a street blocked off by police, hurling stones and chanting slogans.
There were no immediate reports of casualties or arrests.
Witnesses said police fired tear gas and then shots into the air after a march by thousands of PPP backers threatened to turn violent.

Demonstrators burned a flag of the ruling Golkar party before dispersing after 30 minutes, the witnesses said. The PPP supporters complained that Golkar followers had been allowed to parade through the blocked-off street.
The PPP, Golkar and the minority Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) are the only three parties legally entitled to contest Indonesia's May 29 national and local elections.
